text:
Philip Broberg's slap shot on the power play at 8:47 of the third period broke a 1-1 tie and sent STL past WPG 2-1 at Enterprise Center. Broberg also set up the opening goal, a deflection by Jimmy Snuggerud at 12:30 of the first, and finished with a goal, an assist and six shots on goal in 23:42 of ice time. Cole Perfetti had tied it for WPG with a backhand 32 seconds into the third.

STL controlled the early going. In the first period they out-chanced WPG 1.67 to 0.84 in expected goals, a measure of the quality of the shots each team took. The best of them, a 38 percent look for Pavel Buchnevich, was stopped by Stuart Skinner. WPG pushed back as the game went on and finished with 64 shot attempts to 52, but Joel Hofer was ready. He stopped 32 of 33 shots, and by goals saved above expected, which compares what a goalie allowed with what the shots should have produced, he was 1.55 goals better than the shots he faced deserved. Skinner was also good, at 0.97 above expected.

Over the full game, STL's 2.97 expected goals edged WPG's 2.55, and in simulated replays of every shot STL won 58 percent of the time. The result fit the play. STL went 1 for 5 on the power play and WPG went 0 for 3, and the one conversion decided the game. The facts supplied don't include standings, streaks or records, so there is no more to say here about where the result leaves either team.
